Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 27: Ying Chanxi's Luggage

Li Luo spent some time packing up the computer from Ying Chanxi's house.

When he walked out of the study, however, he found that Ying Chanxi was still packing her things.

"Do you really have this much luggage?" Li Luo walked into Ying Chanxi's bedroom and glanced at the floor.

Two large suitcases.

Three large cardboard boxes of the same size.

They completely blocked the walkway by the bed, leaving Li Luo stunned.

"It's not that much, is it?" Ying Chanxi sat on the bed with her legs tucked under her, blinked innocently, and then stuffed folded clothes into a cardboard box. "I only brought a few clothes."

"You call this a few?" Li Luo looked astonished, then couldn't help but say, "With so many clothes, will you even get to wear them all? Won't you be wearing your school uniform every day once school starts?"

"Do you not wear clothes on the weekends?" Ying Chanxi shot him a glare.

"But you still don't need this many, right?" Li Luo looked speechless. "I just brought two sets of pajamas, and three sets of summer clothes like shorts and t-shirts, and nothing else."

He originally couldn't even be bothered to bring pajamas. After all, he usually just slept in his t-shirt, so what was the point of distinguishing between sleepwear and regular clothes?

He only brought them because Lin Xiuhong insisted on stuffing them into his suitcase.

Even so, his suitcase wasn't even full.

But now, looking at Ying Chanxi's luggage, just her clothes alone filled two suitcases and three large cardboard boxes.

Li Luo had no idea where she got so many clothes.

"That's because you're not a picky person," Ying Chanxi huffed. "Girls need to wear pretty clothes to be in a good mood."

Although Ying Chanxi usually wore her uniform to school, she would still wear clothes she liked on the weekends to keep her spirits up.

Li Luo had never noticed this, neither before nor after his rebirth.

It was only now, while packing, that he discovered a girl's wardrobe was truly a bottomless pit.

Where on earth did she get so many clothes?

And this huge stuffed doll!

Li Luo looked at the half-human-sized stuffed panda lying on the desk by the window, already wrapped in transparent plastic.

"You're taking this thing too?" Li Luo couldn't help but ask. "I remember I gave this to you for your elementary school graduation, didn't I? Why do you still have it?"

"None of your business!" Ying Chanxi huffed, then silently hid the small blanket under her butt—the one Li Luo had given her when they were kids—planning to secretly put it in a cardboard box later.

Just as Ying Chanxi continued to pack, Li Luo's phone rang.

He answered, thinking it was his uncle, but it turned out to be Zhao Rongjun.

"Hey, Li Luo, where are you?"

"I'm at home."

"Then why aren't you answering your door? I've been knocking."

"Oh, oh, I'm at the apartment across the hall." Li Luo walked out of Ying Chanxi's bedroom, opened the door, and saw Zhao Rongjun. "You're here."

"I'm here." Zhao Rongjun nodded, then asked with confusion, "Is Ying Chanxi going to the court too?"

"Playing ball isn't urgent." Li Luo coughed twice. "I have a more arduous task for you."

"What?" Zhao Rongjun grew wary. He subconsciously took half a step back, his hand already on the railing of the stairs leading down.

But Li Luo was quicker. With a grin, he grabbed Zhao Rongjun's arm, sidled up to him, and slung an arm around his good brother.

"At the promotion banquet the other day, didn't my dad mention it? My family bought an apartment over by Fuyi High School and planned for me to move in before school starts."

"So?" Zhao Rongjun squinted, having already guessed what was coming.

"It's perfect that you're here. Ying Chanxi and I have almost finished packing our luggage," Li Luo said shamelessly. "My uncle is coming over with his car in a bit, so you can help us move the luggage downstairs."

Lines of frustration appeared on Zhao Rongjun's forehead. He couldn't help but ask, "Then why did you ask me to play ball yesterday?"

"It's all my mom's fault for only telling me about the move today." Li Luo sold out his teammate without a hint of guilt. "The timing just worked out, didn't it?"

"You can help us move, then ride with us to the new place to get familiar with it."

"And then we'll go check out the basketball court at Fuyi High School."

"Can we get in on a weekend?" Zhao Rongjun asked doubtfully.

"Aren't you wearing your uniform?" Li Luo glanced at Zhao Rongjun's uniform, thinking that boys' clothes sure saved fabric, wearing their uniforms even on weekends.

"You don't have a uniform."

"I have my acceptance letter." Li Luo puffed out his chest. "There's nothing wrong with a new student taking a tour of the school ahead of time, right?"

Hearing Li Luo put it that way, Zhao Rongjun reluctantly agreed. "Alright then."

"My good brother!" Li Luo patted Zhao Rongjun's shoulder, extremely satisfied with this free labor he had scored.

Pulling Zhao Rongjun along, Li Luo first moved his own suitcase to the doorway, followed by the computer from the study across the hall.

Then, the two of them helped Ying Chanxi move her packed suitcases and cardboard boxes out.

By the time Ying Chanxi finally finished packing, Li Luo received a perfectly timed call from his uncle.

"Hey! Xiao Luo, I've parked downstairs. Coming up now."

"Got it, Uncle. We're all packed," Li Luo replied, then hung up and made another call to his mom.

"Hello?"

"Mom, we're about to leave."

"Okay," Lin Xiuhong said from the other end. "I'll come over and go with you."

Just as Li Luo finished talking to his mom, a set of footsteps could be heard from downstairs.

A mature and handsome figure appeared in the stairwell.

His uncle, Lin Xiufeng, looked up and saw Li Luo. He raised his eyebrows with a smile, strode up to the fourth floor, and pressed a hand on his head, ruffling his hair vigorously. "You've really made something of yourself! You even got into Fuyi High School."

"Not at all, not at all." Li Luo said modestly, "It's just decent, I guess."

Lin Xiufeng was only thirty-two this year. He had a lean build and slightly long, layered hair styled in the trendy crew cut of the time. He wore a pair of military-style pants and a simple white T-shirt.

He looked very young. Anyone seeing him for the first time would probably assume he was a young man of twenty-five or twenty-six.

There was a nine-year age gap between Li Luo's uncle and Lin Xiuhong; he was a late-in-life child for his maternal grandparents.

When his nephew was just born, Lin Xiufeng was only a little over seventeen, so Li Luo had grown up playing with his uncle, and the two were very close.

However, once Lin Xiufeng got a bit older, his family started pressuring him to get married.

Finding it annoying, he once ran off to another province to work and find his fortune, not returning even once in over half a year.

It wasn't until he was past thirty and his grandparents couldn't be bothered to nag him anymore that Lin Xiuhong, as his older sister, called him back.

Now, Lin Xiufeng worked as a freight driver for a relative's company, driving a large truck every day.

He had been delivering goods to the next city during the promotion banquet, so he had missed it.

However, due to his family connection, he wasn't usually assigned overly tiring work, and his working hours were mostly leisurely.

Today, for instance, Lin Xiufeng had no cargo to transport, so he drove a small company van over to help his nephew move his luggage.

In Li Luo's memory, this uncle of his remained single even into his fifties, much to his grandparents' exasperation.

But he truly doted on Li Luo as a cherished junior member of the family, often taking him out for drinks and skewers, and joking that when he died, all his belongings would be left to him.

When Lin Xiuhong later fell gravely ill, his uncle did everything he could to scrape together money for her, helping his sister with her medical bills until he barely had a penny to his name.

So, seeing his uncle again now, and looking so young and handsome, Li Luo's eyes couldn't help but turn slightly red, though he quickly blinked the feeling away.

At this moment, Ying Chanxi and Zhao Rongjun at the side also politely greeted him.

Lin Xiufeng let out a hearty laugh and greeted the two kids, "Xixi and I go way back. When you were little, you used to chase after Xiao Luo's heels all day long. Look how pretty you are now."

"And Xiao Jun, we used to play ball together all the time, right? I was the one who taught you two basketball."

Having spent a few years drifting in other provinces when he was younger, Lin Xiufeng was very outgoing and quickly hit it off with the youngsters.

The four of them chatted as they moved the luggage downstairs and loaded it into the back of Lin Xiufeng's van.

Ying Chanxi wasn't very strong, so she was in charge of her and Li Luo's schoolbags, while the other three ran up and down two or three times to handle the rest of the luggage.

Soon, Lin Xiuhong also hurried over from the breakfast shop, ready to go with them.

"Is the luggage all packed? Are you missing anything?" Lin Xiuhong asked Li Luo and Ying Chanxi as she got into the front passenger seat.

"We brought everything. If we really forgot something, we can just come back for it later." Li Luo gestured for Zhao Rongjun to get in the van, then followed him into the back seat.

Ying Chanxi got in last and pulled the door shut. Lin Xiufeng started the engine, stepped on the gas, and drove out of Jincheng Community, heading towards Bihai Lanting Community.

...

Yuhang Fuyi High School.

Its full name was Qianjiang University Yuhang City Fuyi High School.

It was backed by the Yin River, and right next to it was the main campus of Qianjiang University.

In its early years, Fuyi High School was an exclusive school for the children of Qianjiang University's teachers and professors.

With economic development and the expansion of compulsory education, Fuyi High School gradually shed its original identity as an affiliated middle school. Relying on its high-quality educational resources, it began to distinguish itself among the high schools in Yuhang City.

In last year's college entrance exams, Fuyi High School was ranked third in Yuhang City, just behind Yuhang No. 2 High School and Xuejun High School.

The number of students admitted to Qingbei University broke double digits for the first time, reaching eleven.

The number of students admitted to Qianjiang University was eighty-one.

And thirty-five students were admitted to other 985 universities in other provinces.

The academic achievements were quite fruitful.

And the apartment that Li Guohong's family had bought was located in the Bihai Lanting Community, right across from Fuyi High School, at 12-1-1502.

At noon.

Xu Youyu, a student from Class One of the second year at Fuyi High School, changed into a white shirt and jeans, went downstairs for lunch, and then strolled back to this rented apartment.

The entire apartment was about 150 square meters. The entrance opened directly into a large living room and balcony.

To the right was a separate piano room, which was previously used by Li Luo's third grand-uncle's cousin for piano practice.

After they moved out, they couldn't be bothered to move the piano, so it was left behind and was now essentially a gift to Li Luo's family.

To the left of the entrance was the kitchen, followed by a small hallway.

Along both sides of the hallway were four doors, leading to two bedrooms, one study, and one bathroom.

The study had been converted into a bedroom, but it was relatively more spacious.

Xu Youyu had rented this study, setting it up with a large desk and her own computer.

At the end of the hallway was the master bedroom of the apartment, which included an en-suite bathroom.

Xu Youyu entered the apartment, changed into her slippers, and went back to her room, closing the door.

She sat down at her desk, rested her chest on the tabletop, and let out a sigh of relief. Then she turned on her computer, went to Qidian Chinese Website, and scrolled through the new book rankings.

Seeing that her *Literary Era* was ranked 31st, Xu Youyu sighed faintly.

Then she logged into her QQ and saw a message from her editor sent that morning.

Qianzhou: Zao Shui, you there? Just a heads-up, your book is scheduled to go premium next Friday. Remember to build up a stockpile of chapters.

Next Friday would be August 22nd... Xu Youyu glanced at the date. There was still about half a month until school started. It would be best to stockpile as many chapters as possible.

After all, starting from the second year of high school, her coursework would get busier, and she couldn't let writing web novels affect her studies.

With this in mind, Xu Youyu replied to her editor.

ZaoShuiHuiZhangGao: Roger.

Qianzhou: This cycle, the most outstanding writers under me are you and Chong Ran. And coincidentally, you both write in the entertainment genre.

Qianzhou: I'll ask Chong Ran in a bit to see if you two can give each other a chapter recommendation.

Qianzhou: Or you could just add each other on QQ. You're both of the same age, so you should have a lot to talk about.

Chong Ran... was that the author of *I'm Really Not a Star*, the book from the same cohort as hers that even made it to Sanjiang?

Wait... Xu Youyu froze for a moment, not quite processing it.

What did "of the same age" mean?
